Pooled result

Estimate withdrawn. Two composites, not one estimand. Registered primaries read from ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-08-19. Fourier (NCT01764633, n=27,564) registers 'Time to Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction, Hospitalization for Unstable Angina, Stroke, or Coronary Revascularization'. Odyssey outcomes (NCT01663402, n=18,924) registers 'Time to First Occurrence of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (mace)', defined in its own description as CHD death, non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal ischaemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalisation. They differ on three axes: fourier counts all cardiovascular death against odyssey's CHD death; Fourier counts all stroke against odyssey's ischaemic stroke; and fourier counts coronary revascularisation, which odyssey does not. Revascularisation is the highest-frequency component in this class of trial, so this is not a rounding difference in the event definition -- it changes what is being counted. P37: composite names are not definitions. Separately, the estimator was DerSimonian-Laird at k=2, and DL is refused below k=10 in this project because its tau-squared is badly biased with few studies. And the object already said so: it carried estimand_established=false and a poolable_reason stating the estimate had been recovered from the page rather than established. Authority: mecir Box 10.10.a C62 -- undertake or display a meta-analysis only if participants, interventions, comparisons and outcomes are judged sufficiently similar to ensure a clinically meaningful answer.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

With two or three studies the Cochrane Handbook (10.10.4.4–10.10.4.5) asks for a sensitivity analysis comparing interval methods rather than a choice between them. Both are given here; the published interval is the first row.

Table 7. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
IntervalMethodSummary (95% CI)
as publishedDerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates0.844 (0.7952 to 0.8959)
sensitivity (Handbook 10.10.4.5)REML with Hartung-Knapp, t on k-1 = 1 degree(s) of freedom (t = 12.7062)0.844 (0.5737 to 1.2418)

The published point is 0.8440 and the house-rule point is 0.8440. The number a reader remembers does not move; what differs is the precision claim. That is why nothing downstream catches this -- every memorable quantity survives.

A floor of 1 is applied to the variance-inflation factor so the adjustment can never narrow an interval below the unadjusted one. That guard is the recognised modification for exactly this instability, and its existence is evidence the small-k behaviour is a known problem with known handling rather than a novel judgement.

Multiple trial-declared outcomes: Time to Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction, Hospitalization for Unstable Angina, Stroke, or Coronary Revascular | Time to First Occurrence of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (mace); Percentage of Observed Participants With Outcome . These 2 trials are not pooled, and the reason is stated rather than the outcome being quietly omitted: Two composites, not one estimand. Registered primaries read from ClinicalTrials.gov 2026-08-19. Fourier (NCT01764633, n=27,564) registers 'Time to Cardiovascular Death, Myocardial Infarction, Hospitalization for Unstable Angina, Stroke, or Coronary Revascularization'. Odyssey outcomes (NCT01663402, n=18,924) registers 'Time to First Occurrence of Major Adverse Cardiovascular Event (mace)', defined in its own description as CHD death, non-fatal MI, fatal and non-fatal ischaemic stroke, or unstable angina requiring hospitalisation. They differ on three axes: fourier counts all cardiovascular death against odyssey's CHD death; Fourier counts all stroke against odyssey's ischaemic stroke; and fourier counts coronary revascularisation, which odyssey does not. Revascularisation is the highest-frequency component in this class of trial, so this is not a rounding difference in the event definition -- it changes what is being counted. P37: composite names are not definitions. Separately, the estimator was DerSimonian-Laird at k=2, and DL is refused below k=10 in this project because its tau-squared is badly biased with few studies. And the object already said so: it carried estimand_established=false and a poolable_reason stating the estimate had been recovered from the page rather than established. NCT01663402ODYSSEY OUTCOMESAlirocumab 75 mg Q2W / up to 150 mg Q2W (treatment, n=9462) vs Placebo (control, n=9462) [+2 further fields recorded on the object] Alirocumab 75 mg Q2W / up to 150 mg Q2W (label_corrected): Labels swapped, arithmetic correct -- corrected 2026-08-18. Settled by the denominators, which are unambiguous: Odyssey outcomes reports 903 events on alirocumab and 1052 on placebo. This object carried arms[0] labelled "Placebo" with n=13784 (evolocumab's denominator) and arms[1] labelled "Evolocumab" with n=13780. The counts were in intervention-first order and the labels in registry order, and nothing compared the two. The pooled effect 0.8445 is correct and unchanged: it was computed from the counts, which were right. Only the description was wrong. Mirror image of the fcm-hf defect, where the labels were right and the arithmetic read position. Both are position-is-not-a-role.not extracted

Settled by the denominators, which are unambiguous: Fourier randomised 13784 to evolocumab and 13780 to placebo.
